title: Don't guess (Avot 1:16)
hook: Gamaliel: find a teacher, free yourself of doubt, don't tithe by guesswork
carry: someone else's share was in the pile

segments.voice: Yesterday, say little: Shammai, and Abraham's morsel of bread that turned into a feast. Your line was just a morsel of bread. Day two hundred forty-six.

Dinner with six friends, one check. Somebody says, let's just call it about forty each. Nobody pulls out a calculator. Somewhere at the table, the person who only had soup is quietly paying for someone else's steak, and the one who had the steak is quietly relieved. Nobody meant any harm. It was just a guess. Today's sage worried about exactly that kind of guess, only his table was a farmer's harvest, and the people who went short were the poor.
screen: `ONE CHECK, SIX FRIENDS.` → `LET'S CALL IT FORTY EACH.` → `A HARVEST, AND THE POOR.`

segments.voice: The chain now reaches Rabban Gamaliel, called the Elder. Tradition says he was Hillel's grandson, and the Mishnah gives him the title Rabban, our master. His saying: make for yourself a teacher, remove yourself from doubt, and don't tithe by estimate too often. That last line needs a picture. In the land of Israel, parts of a farmer's harvest weren't his to keep. Some went to the priests, a tenth to the Levites, and in certain years a tenth to the poor. So a farmer stands in front of a heap of grain. He can measure it, or eyeball it and say, that's about a tenth. The commentators point out that a guess goes wrong both ways. Too little, and he keeps what belonged to someone else. Too much, and what he set aside isn't a proper tithe. Either way, he's living with doubt. Now the first two lines make sense. Make for yourself a teacher: Pirkei Avot already said this, back with Joshua ben Perachyah. Some commentators say that one was about learning, and this one is about decisions: when you don't know, ask someone who does, instead of making it up. And remove yourself from doubt: don't leave important things resting on a shrug. It's a small, practical saying that reaches a long way. Guessing feels easier than measuring. But when other people's share is in the pile, the easy guess costs somebody something.
screen: `RABBAN GAMALIEL THE ELDER.` · `A HEAP OF GRAIN, A TENTH.` · `A GUESS GOES WRONG BOTH WAYS.` · `ASK A TEACHER, LEAVE THE DOUBT.` · then, large: `DON'T GUESS.`

segments.voice: Count each breath, in and out as one, and really count instead of estimating: one, two, three. If you lose track, don't round up; go back to one. It's harder than it sounds, and that's the point: attention is a kind of measuring.
Don't guess. Rabban Gamaliel's rule: find a teacher, step out of doubt, and measure what belongs to others instead of eyeballing it.
Your line: someone else's share was in the pile. A tenth is a number, not a feeling. Day two hundred forty-six, done.

howItsDone: Observant Jews in the land of Israel still separate tithes (ma'aser) from produce, and when a question of Jewish law comes up, many ask a rabbi rather than decide by guesswork.

original.note: Mishnaic Hebrew: don't tithe by estimates too often.

trapdoor: what you thought: a rule about math.
what it means: when other people's share is involved, measure and ask, don't shrug and guess.
what a scholar hears: Gamaliel's word is umadot, estimates, and the commentators say a tithe set aside by eyeballing can fail in either direction.
guess: measure and ask, when others' share depends on it
trust your gut, since first instincts are best
never decide anything without total certainty
recall: giving people the benefit of the doubt

notes: Some commentators and scholars identify the Gamaliel of Avot 1:16 as Rabban Gamaliel the Elder; others discuss whether it could be a later Gamaliel. Confirm the identification and 'Hillel's grandson' (tradition; some sources say son of Simeon, son of Hillel).
'First sage called Rabban': commonly stated; confirm.
The explanation that an overestimated tithe is also defective follows Bartenura and others on this mishnah; confirm the wording.
The reading that 1:6 is about learning and 1:16 about rulings in law follows Bartenura (and others); confirm.
Tithe portions simplified: terumah for priests, first tithe for Levites, poor tithe in the third and sixth years; confirm.
